subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: Should shared OAuth refresh retry transient provider/plugin refresh failures by default, and what retryable-error classifier and retry budget should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this auth-provider behavior can change failure timing, mask terminal auth errors, and interact with provider-owned refresh hooks, so maintainer intent is needed before automation encodes policy.

options.title: Approve bounded shared retry
options.body: Use retryAsync around the shared refresh attempt with a narrow transient-error classifier, small bounded budget, and tests for success-after-retry, retry exhaustion, and non-retryable OAuth failures.

options.title: Keep retries provider-owned
options.body: Leave the shared auth manager single-shot and require providers with known transient refresh behavior to implement their own refreshOAuth retry policy.

options.title: Defer until live proof
options.body: Keep the issue open but require live upstream transient-failure evidence before selecting a generic retry policy.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded shared retry
recommendation.body: Use retryAsync around the shared refresh attempt with a narrow transient-error classifier, small bounded budget, and tests for success-after-retry, retry exhaustion, and non-retryable OAuth failures.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc authored the central OAuth lifecycle manager that would own the shared retry placement and interaction with existing locks/fallbacks.
